s1.syndrome_frame: Painless mass on the frontal bone with a 2-month history and associated radiographic findings
salient_findings: Painless mass on the right side of the frontal bone
Lytic lesion of the frontal bone with a soap-bubble appearance on CT
Lobulated frontal-bone mass with avid enhancement on MRI
key_facts: 50-year-old man
2-month history of a painless mass
Mass located on the right side of the frontal bone
Mass measured approximately 4.0 × 3.5 cm
Mass was well circumscribed, soft, nonmobile, and non-tender
Laboratory studies were unremarkable
Neurologic examination was unremarkable
Plain radiography showed a large, circumscribed radiolucent lesion
CT showed cortical destruction of the inner and outer tables
MRI showed a lobulated mass that was hypointense on T1-weighted images and hyperintense on T2-weighted images

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Soap-bubble appearance on radiography and lytic lesion with cortical destruction on CT are characteristic of giant cell tumor

shortlist.label: Hemangioma of the bone
shortlist.why_kept: Lobulated mass with avid enhancement on MRI and soap-bubble appearance on radiography are consistent with hemangioma

shortlist.label: Osteoma
shortlist.why_kept: Well-circumscribed, radiolucent lesion on plain radiography could be an osteoma, although less likely given the size and soft-tissue component

shortlist.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Expansile, lytic lesion with fluid-fluid levels on MRI could be an aneurysmal bone cyst, although the clinical presentation is atypical

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Ground-glass appearance on radiography and cortical thinning on CT could be seen in fibrous dysplasia, although the clinical and imaging features are not typical

raw.rationale: The soap-bubble appearance on CT and the presence of a well-circumscribed, soft, and non-tender mass are characteristic of hemangioma of the bone.

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor
rejected.why: Giant cell tumors are typically more aggressive and may have a softer, more lytic appearance on imaging, but the presence of cortical destruction is less common in hemangiomas than in giant cell tumors

rejected.label: Osteoma
rejected.why: Osteomas are typically small, well-defined, and composed of compact bone, which does not match the large, lytic lesion described

rejected.label: Aneurysmal bone cyst
rejected.why: Aneurysmal bone cysts often have a more fluid-filled, expansile appearance on imaging and may be tender, which does not match the description of the mass

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: Fibrous dysplasia often has a ground-glass appearance on radiographs and may be associated with cafe-au-lait spots or other systemic features, which are not mentioned in the vignette
